Toy multiSimmap of biogeographic ranges

Source: R/dataset_doc.R
toy_multiSimmap_ranges.Rd

Set of 10 stochastic character maps (multiSimmap) of phylograftR::toy_backbone for the biogeographic ranges of phylograftR::toy_tip_data, coded as in BioGeoBEARS (areas "A", "B" and "C"; ranges of at most two areas). Each map is one possible biogeographic history, with anagenetic changes of range along the branches and cladogenetic events at the nodes.

They were inferred from the tip data with the DEC model of BioGeoBEARS (the only model fit), through deepSTRAPP::prepare_trait_data() (see vignette("prepare_stochastic_maps")): biogeographic stochastic mapping (BSM) was run, and its output converted into stochastic maps (seed 3456). 100 maps were simulated, and only the first 10 are kept to keep the package light. 10 maps are enough for illustration, but actual analyses should use more maps (100 or more).

The ranges of the maps include the ranges of the tips and may include other ranges only found at the internal nodes (e.g., "C" or "AC"). Use treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE to use the areas as allowed states in the grafting functions (see vignette("biogeographic_data")).

Usage

data(toy_multiSimmap_ranges)

Format

An object of classes "multiSimmap" and "multiPhylo": a list of 10 objects of class "simmap", with the same tips, topology and branch lengths as phylograftR::toy_backbone.

See also

Other datasets and functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::toy_tip_data for the tip data used to build the maps.

  • phylograftR::toy_simmap_ranges for a single map of ranges.

  • phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_ranges for missing taxa with allowed ranges.

Examples

# Import the data
data(toy_multiSimmap_ranges)

# Ranges found in the first map
colnames(toy_multiSimmap_ranges[[1]]$mapped.edge)
#> [1] "_"  "A"  "B"  "C"  "AB" "AC" "BC"
